newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GM's Opel Belgium 1996 profit crumbles.
newsitem.headline: GM's Opel Belgium 1996 profit crumbles.

text.p: Opel Belgium, the Antwerp-based assembly unit of U.S. car maker General Motors, said on Monday that its net profit fell to 85 million francs ($2.4 million) in 1996 from 878 million a year earlier despite a 5.7 percent rise in turnover.
It said in a statement that 1996 earnings were strongly influenced by high investment costs and feelings that a real recovery of the western economy was not materialising.

Spokesman Dirk Snauwaert said the company also made a provision of 638 million francs related to a European Commission ban on Belgian schemes, called Maribel, which allow exporters facing international competition to pay reduced social security contributions.

The Commission had ruled that previous Maribel schemes violated EU fair competition rules, but has accepted a new plan which it said involved general measures to preserve blue-collar work rather than sectoral schemes.
Snauwaert said the Maribel saga would raise eyebrows at the Opel headquarters as it showed there were no steady regulations which made it difficult for Opel to draw up a long-term strategy.
"Hopefully the Belgian government will work out a solution," he said.
Snauwaert added that the company also suffered from a four-day strike in March 1996.
"Without all this (Maribel and the strike), we would have been at a normal level of profit," Snauwaert said.
Turnover rose to 48.3 billion francs from 45.7 billion.
Opel Belgium has invested about 15 billion francs in the past five years, of which 5.5 billion in 1996, to modernise its Antwerp plant which has a workforce of 7,775.
Opel Belgium president and managing director Leo Valvekens said in the statement that the company was planning to invest another 7.4 billion francs in 1997.
Snauwaert said this was mainly earmarked for "future product programmes" but declined to give further details.
Opel Belgium produced 295,454 cars in 1996 against 304,505 in 1995 and 319,000 in 1994. It assembled 182,160 Opel Astras and 113,294 Vectras.
The company has already produced more than 10 million cars.
The plant exports 94 percent of its output to more than 50 countries. Germany is its main market, importing between 40 and 45 percent of production in Antwerp.
The Antwerp plant is the second-largest of GM's 12 production units in Europe behind Zaragoza which produced 436,400 Corsas and Tigras.
It is also a major producer of car components
